analysis: All three changed files are test-only. The changes are mechanical API-compatibility updates for a dependency bump. The stub LanguageModel.prepare signature moves from (windowSize:) to (state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters) at ReserveRaisePreflightTests.swift:254 and GLM5NextLocalLoadPolicyTests.swift:614. The Gemma4TextConfiguration decode is qualified as MLXLLM.Gemma4TextConfiguration at SlotSizingDriftTests.swift:185, which resolves a name ambiguity. No production source changed. I found no change to the attestation, authorization, encryption, key handling, cache storage (T-041), coordinator wire contract, or fan helper boundaries. The stubs throw or return trivial values and touch no secrets, network, or persistent state. The tests write only seeded fake snapshots to the HF cache and clean them up; this behavior is unchanged. The one remaining question is outside the supplied evidence. The dependency bump that changes the LanguageModel protocol (prefill parameters, LMOutput.State) is not shown. Its production security effects on the inference engine (TB-007) and the prefix cache (T-041) belong to whichever batch contains those files. Nothing in these test diffs invalidates a threat-model assumption.
